environment.scan_execution_context: direct scanner import per job; no FastAPI, no database, no auth

scenarios.description: Single page, clean fixture (production single-page path with screenshots)
Single page, issue-dense fixture WITH screenshot capture (production single-page path)
Single page, issue-dense fixture with _attach_issue_screenshots patched to a no-op
Single page, JS-rendered SPA fixture (violations injected via setTimeout)
Multi-page crawl, 5 pages, crawl_depth=2, request_delay_ms=0 (production worker path: browser analysis per page)
Multi-page crawl, 5 pages, crawl_depth=2, request_delay_ms=250 (production default delay)

methodology.scenario_definition: one iteration = one full scan_page() job; per-call scenarios create and close a BrowserSession per job, worker-mode scenarios reuse one BrowserSession across all measured jobs (the optimized worker shape)
methodology.iterations_note: measured iterations exclude the warm-up; single-page scenarios use 7, multi-page scenarios use 5 (each multi iteration scans 5 pages)
methodology.percentile_method: linear interpolation between closest ranks (numpy/Excel PERCENTILE.INC)

phase_notes.browser_setup: BrowserSession.new_page(): lazy Playwright/Chromium start on first page + new browser context + new page
phase_notes.axe_core: axe_scanner.run_axe_core(): inject axe-core script + axe.run() in the page
phase_notes.screenshots_total: _attach_issue_screenshots(): capture and store one screenshot per unique selector
phase_notes.fetch_html: _fetch_page_html(): urllib raw-HTML fetch (fallback / multi when browser analysis is off)
phase_notes.prepare_html: _prepare_html_for_screenshot(): script stripping / base-tag injection (fallback browser path)
phase_notes.nested:context_create: nested in browser_setup: browser.new_context(viewport, locale, UA)
phase_notes.nested:fixed_settle_wait: nested in render_wait: page.wait_for_timeout(page_timeout_ms//40 clamped to 250-600ms)
phase_notes.nested:axe_script_fetch: nested in axe_core: axe-core 4.10.2 CDN download (first call per process only)
phase_notes.nested:screenshot_capture: nested in screenshots_total: locator scroll/bounding-box + page.screenshot
phase_notes.nested:screenshot_store: nested in screenshots_total: Cloudinary upload or base64 data-URL conversion

fixtures./clean: clean small page (production single-page path, 0 expected violations)
fixtures./issue-dense: issue-dense page equivalent to GET /test/page-bad (~10-15 violations)
fixtures./spa: JS-rendered SPA equivalent to GET /test/page-js-rendered (violations injected after 150ms)
fixtures./multi/: multi-page fixture root linking 5 pages with fixed known violations

important_notes: Per-call scenarios launch and close their own Playwright driver + Chromium browser per job (the baseline production lifecycle).

Worker-mode scenarios use one BrowserSession across all measured scans; the strategy is recorded per scenario (native session injection when scan_page supports browser_session, otherwise an emulated shared-session factory for the baseline code).
The browser_start cost of worker mode appears once in the warm-up sample (and in worker_session metadata), not in the measured samples.

single_render_failure_fallback forces the rendered attempt to fail while the browser is available: this is the raw-HTML + browser-analysis fallback path affected by the fixed _run_playwright_analysis defect; before the fix it returned custom-check-only issues.
Fixtures are served from 127.0.0.1 over plain HTTP so target-network latency is effectively zero; real-world URLs will be slower.
axe-core script is cached in a module global after the first fetch; warm scenarios do not include the CDN download.
CLOUDINARY_URL is unset for this run, so screenshots are stored as inline base64 data URLs (portable CPU cost); production with Cloudinary configured pays network upload cost instead.
issue counts are recorded per scenario so timings can be interpreted as work done (ms/page, ms/issue).
